## Summary

The IEEE registry lists 16 MA-L blocks to "Lenovo Mobile Communication
Technology Ltd." at No. 999 Qishan North 2nd Road in the Xiamen Torch
Hi-tech zone, Fujian, and two further blocks to a separate Wuhan entity,
Lenovo Mobile Communication (Wuhan) Company Limited [2]. Lenovo, founded
in Beijing in 1984, names Xiamen among its research centres in mainland
China, and its smartphone and tablet division was sold in 2008 and
bought back in 2009 [1]. Lenovo phones were sold as the LePhone in China
and IdeaPhone overseas, in lines such as the Vibe and K series, and in
August 2015 Lenovo announced that its phone business apart from ZUK
would fold into Motorola Mobility [3]. Motorola Mobility, owned by
Lenovo since October 2014, subsumed Lenovo's smartphone division and
sells the Edge, Razr and Moto G lines [4].

A MAC in these blocks is therefore most likely a Lenovo-branded Android
phone or tablet, mostly of the pre-Motorola-merger era; the link from
this Xiamen registrant to those products is inferred from the name, not
stated by a source consulted [1][3]. Android 10 and later uses a
persistent randomized MAC per network by default, so older phones from
these blocks would expose the burned-in address [5]. Founding date,
radios, chipsets and FCC grantee codes are not listed: no source
consulted names this entity directly, and the FCC ID databases refused
the session that wrote this entry.
